premise_verification.verdict: PREMISE HOLDS AT THE SHIPPED-LIBRARY ENTRY POINT AND FAILS AT THE ENTRY POINT THE CORPUS ACTUALLY MEASURES. 'Rejected local close' is NOT one uniform case: the pinned 1.6.0 tree has two local-close entry points that disagree with each other, and the coordinator's brief conflated them. derive.go does NOT disagree with Java; it agrees with the Java path the oracle actually executes.

entry_point_A_shipped_library.site: WebSocketImpl.java:463-507 close(int code, String message, boolean remote)
entry_point_A_shipped_library.reading: From OPEN with a non-1006 code and a TWOWAY draft, :472-487 builds the close frame inside a try block (new CloseFrame(); setReason; setCode; isValid(); sendFrame at :482-486). CloseFrame.isValid (framing/CloseFrame.java:226-243) throws for a reserved code — the 'closecode must not be sent over the wire' InvalidFrameException at framing/CloseFrame.java:241. That exception is CAUGHT at WebSocketImpl.java:488, which logs, calls onWebsocketError, and calls flushAndClose(CloseFrame.ABNORMAL_CLOSE, "generated frame is invalid", false) at :491. flushAndClose (:584-606) sets closecode/closemessage/closedremotely, flips flushandclosestate, calls onWriteDemand and onWebsocketClosing, and RETURNS — it never calls closeConnection, so readyState is not set to CLOSED. Control then reaches the method's unconditional tail at :503, readyState = ReadyState.CLOSING.
entry_point_A_shipped_library.conclusion: CONFIRMED: via this entry point a rejected local close DOES end in CLOSING. The brief's citation of :488-503 is correct for this path.
additional_paths_checked_not_one_uniform: code == ABNORMAL_CLOSE (1006) from OPEN: :466-471 sets readyState = CLOSING at :468 and RETURNS at :470 — it reaches CLOSING WITHOUT ever building or validating a CloseFrame, so it is not a 'rejection' path at all even though close_code_rejection(1006, …) rejects in the port.

readyState NOT OPEN (NOT_YET_CONNECTED): :495-501 runs the flush ladder (FLASHPOLICY / PROTOCOL_ERROR / NEVER_CONNECTED) and then also falls to :503 CLOSING. No CloseFrame is built, so the validity chain never runs on this arm.
readyState already CLOSING or CLOSED: the :464 guard makes the whole method a no-op.
closeConnection (:530-567) and eot (:608-624) were read to confirm flushAndClose does not synchronously reach CLOSED and therefore cannot be overwritten by :503.

entry_point_B_pinned_oracle_adapter.reading: Declares 'throws ProtocolException, InvalidDataException'. It calls requireOpen, then constructs the CloseFrame ITSELF — new CloseFrame(); setCode(code); setReason(reason); frame.isValid() at OracleEngine.java:470 — and does NOT wrap that call. The same InvalidDataException therefore PROPAGATES OUT of the method. WebSocketImpl.close is never invoked and its line 503 is never reached, so emitOutbound (:471), the close-detail assignment (:472), the close_initiated event (:473) and transition(State.CLOSING, …) (:474) are all skipped.
entry_point_B_pinned_oracle_adapter.state_variable_caveat_disclosed: OracleEngine does instantiate a real WebSocketImpl (OracleEngine.java:307), but the response's final_state is serialized from the adapter's own 'private enum State { OPEN, CLOSING, CLOSED }' (OracleEngine.java:263) at OracleEngine.java:578 and :602 — NOT from socket.getReadyState(). Stated plainly: the live corpus does not directly observe WebSocketImpl.readyState at this action. What it observes is the real jar's isValid rejection plus the adapter's own state, and that pair is the plane's designated behavioral authority for corpus actions.
entry_point_B_pinned_oracle_adapter.conclusion: CONFIRMED: via the entry point the corpus measures, a rejected local close does NOT reach CLOSING.

derive_go_comparison.self_described_authority: The function's own doc comment reads 'sendClose mirrors OracleEngine.sendClose over CloseFrame.setCode (which normalizes 1015 to 1005), setReason, and isValid' — it names OracleEngine, NOT WebSocketImpl, as the thing it mirrors.
derive_go_comparison.behavior: Applies the 1015->1005 normalization, then closeIsValidRejection (derive.go:618-634); on rejection it returns javaInvalid(failCode) at derive.go:900 BEFORE emitOutbound, so no frame, no close detail, no close_initiated event, and NO transition. The transition to closing is at derive.go:910, downstream of the rejection return.
derive_go_comparison.agreement_verdict: derive.go AGREES with OracleEngine.sendClose (entry point B) and with the live transcript. It DISAGREES with WebSocketImpl.close (entry point A). So the port did not 'follow derive.go instead of Java' — it follows the Java path the oracle executes. The two authorities do not disagree with each other; two different Java call sites disagree with each other, and derive.go tracks the correct one for this action.
derive_go_comparison.correction_to_the_brief: The owner decision's context field says 'the port follows derive.go, its named fidelity authority' as if that were an alternative to following Java. honesty_notes: IMPLEMENTED IS FALSE. The owner-mandated behavior change is NOT in the committed tree. The mandate was executed to completion and then reverted under the decision's own escape clause; nobody should read this receipt as 'the port now matches Java on rejected closes'.

The brief's premise is HALF RIGHT and the half that is wrong matters. WebSocketImpl.java:488-503 really does reach CLOSING. But 'rejected local close' is not one uniform case, and the case the corpus measures runs through OracleEngine.sendClose, which never calls WebSocketImpl.close at all.

derive.go and the shipped Java source do NOT disagree in the way the decision's context field implies. derive.go's own doc comment names OracleEngine.sendClose as what it mirrors, and it mirrors it correctly. The disagreement is between two Java entry points.

The live 'final_state' is the oracle adapter's state enum (OracleEngine.java:263, serialized at :578/:602), not a direct read of WebSocketImpl.readyState. The conflict is real and gate-level, but this receipt does not claim anyone watched a live WebSocketImpl stay OPEN.

error.detail differs between Rust and live Java on us005.pub.0000 (and on 25 other cases) both before and after the change. That is the pre-existing, documented, non-semantic diagnostic-wording difference the evaluator never compares — it is NOT a divergence introduced here, and it is stated so it is not mistaken for one.

Autobahn was re-run for 7.* ONLY, at the final reverted tree. The full-suite figures in the brief (233/11/3/0, 246/247) are carried forward from E5b UNRE-EXECUTED by this lane. No Autobahn case exercises the rejected-local-close arm, so the run proves non-regression and nothing more.

The close model is reported as REQUIRING RE-RUN. It was not re-run, and no file under assurance/formal was modified. The handoff note reverses E3's recorded 'invert it' instruction, which is a substantive change to another lane's plan and needs coordinator routing rather than silent adoption.

I ran corporactl evaluate --tier handshake against the Rust harness output and got 49 failures before realizing it was the wrong tool for that transcript format. Disclosed above rather than dropped from the record.

assurance/concurrency/plan.json was edited by hand (its ledger head/count binding and the surrounding prose). The gate requires that binding to track the ledger, and no generator owns that file; the ledger bytes themselves were produced only by cmd/deltaledgerctl.

Two regeneration flags were used, both sanctioned by the brief and both re-verified without the flag afterwards. No gate was bypassed, skipped, or loosened, and no test was weakened — in particular send_close_invalid_code_rejects_without_a_frame was NOT edited to accommodate the change.
blockers: OWNER DECISION REQUIRED: rejected-close-transition-divergence cannot be satisfied as written. Matching shipped WebSocketImpl.close costs the live-Java public-corpus differential (74/74 -> 73/74 on us005.pub.0000). The owner should choose among: (a) ACCEPT the escape clause, keep the port as-is, and treat delta-9dd3ab86 as the resolution — the option this lane took and the only one requiring no further work; (b) re-scope the mandate to the LIBRARY-level close entry point only, i.e. leave the corpus-facing send_close command alone and add a separate WebSocketImpl.close-faithful close API above or beside it, which changes no live-confirmed observable; or (c) re-baseline the corpus expectation for us005.pub.0000, which would require re-running the pinned Java oracle and is the only option that touches live-recorded evidence.

E3 ROUTING REQUIRED: assurance/formal currently instructs a future reader to invert RejectedSendDoesNotTransition when the port change lands. That instruction is now wrong and will mislead whoever reads it next. The precise edits are in chain_results.4_close_model_handoff.e3_handoff_note and must be routed to the E3 lane after both branches merge.
